NARRATIVE AND PLANS FOR TYPE 1 ZONING AMENDMENT FOR
4634-36 NORTH AVERS AVENUE, CHICAGO IL

The subject property consists of 2 lots: the lot at 4636 N. Avers is improved with an older
residential building with two dwelling units, and the lot at 4634 N. Avers is currently vacant. Both
lots were previously under common ownership. The Applicant intends to develop the vacant lot
with a new two-story single-family house. The existing two-flat at 4636 N. Avers will remain as
is, The existing two-flat at 4636 North Avers needs a zoning change to an RT4 District with
optional variation relief for the setbacks, to comply with Section 17-17-0301 Division of
Improved Zoning Lots, and related standards and the bulk requirements of the Ordinance, so that
the vacant lot at 4634 N. Avers is a separate buildable zoning lot under the RS3 District, while the
existing two-flat at 4636 N. Avers remains as is, at its current location, on a single lot.

Project 4636 North Avers:

Description: Zoning Change from the RS3 Residential Single-Unit (Detached
House) District to the RT4 Residential Two-Flat, Townhouse and
Multi-Unit District.

4634 North Avers:

Zoning Change from the RS3 Residential Single-Unit (Detached
House) District to an RS3 Residential Single-Unit (Detached House)
District.

L Optional Relief for Adjustment and Variation under Section 17-13-0303-D —

a Type 1 map amendment pursuant to Section 17-13-0300, may include relief available
pursuant to Section 17-13-1000 or 17-13-1100; in such instances, City Council approval of a
Type-1 application containing said elements shall preclude subsequent review otherwise
required pursuant to Sections 17-13-1000 or 17-13-1100, provided that no Type 1
application permits issued may be in violation of Section 17-13-0310:.

(A) | The Applicant also seeks relief for variations under section 17-13-1101-B, from side
setback requirements of Section 17-2-0309-A to reduce the combined side setbacks from
5’ required to 2.87’ existing (with 0’ on the south and 2.87’ on the north); and to reduce
the front setback requirements per Section 17-2-0305-A from 15.73’ required to 13.32’
existing, in order for the existing two-flat at 4636 North Avers to remain, as is, with these
existing setbacks, on a single 25’ lot.

(B) _ Inaddition, the Applicant is requesting all relief necessary, as allowed by the Code, to
comply with Section 17-17-0301 Division of Improved Zoning Lots, and related standards
and the bulk requirements of the Ordinance, so that the vacant lot at 4634 N. Avers is a
separate buildable zoning lot, to be improved with the proposed single family house per
the attached Type | Plans, while the existing two-flat at 4636 N. Avers remains as is, at its
current location on a single 25’ wide lot, with the existing setbacks, per the attached Type
1 Plans.

In support of this request, the Applicant states the following:

1. Strict compliance with the regulations of this Zoning Ordinance would create practical
difficulties and hardships for the subject property, since without the relief requested, the
Applicant’s vacant lot remains unbuildable and unmarketable. The southern wall of existing two-
flat is setback 1.6’, the 0’ setback relates to its bay window overhang.

2. The requested variation is consistent with the stated purpose and intent of this Zoning
Ordinance since this proposed redevelopment and corresponding variations are compatible with
the existing land use pattern on the block, which exhibits similar reduced setbacks. The new
single-family house will increase the variety of available housing stock, in response to the
growing housing demand in the neighborhood.

Final for Publication

3. Evidence of Practical Difficulties or Particular Hardship is as follows:

- The property in question cannot yield a reasonable return if permitted to be used only in
accordance with the strict standards of this Zoning Ordinance since without the relief requested
the vacant lot remains unbuildable and unmarketable.

- The practical difficulties and particular hardships are due to unique circumstances and are
not generally applicable to other similarly situated properties. The requested variations are needed
to allow division of an improved zoning lot. The relief requested allows for the vacant parcel to
be buildable.

- These variations will not alter the essential character of the neighborhood, since the
proposed single-family house has been designed in strict compliance with the Ordinance;
moreover, this proposed redevelopment has been designed to follow the existing land use pattern
on the block.
